scope: Synthetic V1 primary-care encounter v2 source; exact text-to-facts and exported SOAP review. Not a physician gold standard or treatment recommendation.
method: Read v2 raw transcript and compared each extracted fact, primary source span, speaker, qualifiers/action state and exported V1-soap.json display row. Reviewed source-first coverage and explicitly compared material v1 defects. No model/API/network calls.

findings.finding: Prior PT nonattendance and prior knee injection denial are explicit in the source but absent as distinct historical facts and S statements. Current noncompletion and no injection during this encounter are narrower/different claims.

Continuation of lisinopril, decision not to add an oral anti-inflammatory, and three clinician activity recommendations are in A rather than P; the P section therefore omits these otherwise extracted plan details.
No payer authorization decision is a Doctor-stated administrative event with unknown experiencer; SOAP S is an unsuitable section, although the prior patient-speaker error is gone.

Machine marked actual acetaminophen doses as source_insufficient_evidence for execution, but the primary source explicitly reports doses taken on four separate days. Retain as patient-reported use without independent administration certification.
Rest as ongoing and mild relief as completed are interpretive action labels; the source supports patient-reported help but not a discrete treatment course.

The ending paragraph now has an explicit Doctor label. The five extracted ending facts cite Doctor, and the exported SOAP no longer says the patient reported those acts or administrative status. The explicit no-PT-during-visit sentence is not separately extracted.

No materially false dose, vital sign, test result, completed therapy, confirmed imaging diagnosis, or new clinical event identified in the 106 quoted assertions. This does not establish clinical accuracy or exhaustiveness.
